claims.claim: As of 2026-10-06, the former $800 duty-free de minimis treatment cannot be assumed for China-to-US consumer parcels; the new postal informal-entry rule became effective July 24, 2026.
claims.counterevidence: The postal rule contains transition provisions and route-specific entry procedures, so it must not be applied as one universal per-parcel fee formula.

claims.claim: FY2027 CBP fees effective October 1, 2026 include $2.77 for automated informal entry not prepared by CBP, up to $1.38 per express-consignment waybill, and formal MPF limits of $34.58 to $670.86 at an unchanged 0.3464% rate; Section 301 duties were not eliminated by EO 14389.
claims.counterevidence: These fees are entry-mode specific and must not all be summed for every parcel.

claims.claim: Superbuy currently publishes zero standard purchasing-service fees for Taobao, Tmall, JD and 1688, free parcel consolidation, and final international freight reconciliation based on final parcel data and the logistics provider invoice.
claims.counterevidence: Domestic freight, international freight, customs costs, value-added services and other route fees remain.

claims.claim: Superbuy shipping economics depend materially on package dimensions and item restrictions; one published rule uses the greater of actual and volumetric weight with L*W*H/6000 when a side is at least 60 cm, and battery acceptance is route-specific.
claims.counterevidence: Not every carrier or route uses the same divisor or 60 cm rule.

claims.claim: The current public Superbuy package feed contains USA observations including CNY78 at 750g, CNY352.8 at 2510g, CNY393.2 at 2850g, CNY433.6 at 3636g and CNY597.2 at 3177g, but these are not valid SKU-specific ZIP10001 quotations.
claims.counterevidence: The feed omits packed dimensions, destination ZIP, complete contents and customs assumptions.

claims.claim: Superbuy Business Service publicly describes dropshipping and splitting orders so parcels can be shipped separately to different end users.
claims.counterevidence: The business-service page could not be opened as a normal full text page in this session, so the evidence is indexed-page content rather than a fully opened page.

claims.claim: BuckyDrop publishes a CNY9.90 per-parcel fulfillment fee, CNY2 per additional piece above five, CNY2/kg overweight surcharge above 8kg, and an API-enabled direct fulfillment workflow.
claims.counterevidence: Its zero-markup shipping and carrier-rate statements are company claims and do not supply a current ZIP10001 carrier quote.

claims.claim: Sugargoo's published workflow uses destination, product category, weight and dimensions and reconciles estimated shipping with final packed weight or volume; route capacity and timing can vary.
claims.counterevidence: Sugargoo official blog pages returned 403 when directly opened in this session, and historical route prices are too stale for a 2026-10-06 landed-cost calculation.

claims.claim: A 2026 Sugargoo community case demonstrates that volumetric pricing can radically change cost: an 8001g parcel measuring 74x50x34 cm was confirmed by a Sugargoo account as 21.25kg billable weight under a /6000 rule.
claims.counterevidence: This is a single anecdotal shipment and cannot establish an average or median surcharge.

claims.claim: Commercial aggregation of 1000 separately fulfilled consumer orders appears operationally possible without physical consolidation, but no public evidence establishes a specific 1000-order freight discount or threshold.
claims.counterevidence: A confidential commercial contract could contain meaningful rate tiers that are not publicly visible.

claims.claim: All 54 frozen SKUs could be classified for logistics risk, but none had sufficient packed weight, dimensions, route quotation and HTS data for an auditable ZIP10001 exact landed-shipping calculation.
claims.counterevidence: Warehouse rehearsal data or a complete current quote could immediately make individual SKUs numerically evaluable.

claims.claim: Public evidence is insufficient to determine Superbuy's revenue mix or to assert that its main profit source is a freight markup.
claims.counterevidence: Non-public financials or logistics contracts could reveal a freight margin that is not disclosed on the consumer fee page.
